newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia detains seven left-wing activists.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia detains seven left-wing activists.

text.p: Indonesian police have arrested seven activists of the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) in a continuing crackdown on activists since the July riots, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Saturday.
The paper quoted Central Java Police Chief Major-General Harimas as saying on Thursday that the PRD activists were detained while holding a clandestine meeting.
The government has accused the PRD of being behind the July 27 riots, said to be the worst in Jakarta in more than 20 years.
Activist sources said the seven were detained in Semarang, Java's third biggest city, on September 9.
The report quoted Harimas as saying some of the activists might be sent to Jakarta for further questioning.

He said two of those detained - I Gusti Agung Anom Astika and a man he identified as Wilson - were believed to be core members of the PRD's executive board and had long been on the authorities' wanted list.
The others - Wirayanti, Aan Rusdianto, Hari Sutanto, Nurleili Huda and Stevanus - were members of student and labour organisations under the PRD, the report said.
Activist sources said on Saturday it was thought the five had been released but Anom and Wilson had been handed over to another security agency.
PRD leader Budiman Sudjatmiko and nine colleagues have been in detention in Jakarta since last month. They face subversion charges which carry the maximum penalty of death.
The government has blamed the PRD for being behind the riots in which the official human rights commission says five people died and 74 were reported missing.
The PRD is not among the three parties allowed to contest parliamentary elections in Indonesia.
